answer: Reputation follows an exponential temporal half-life: trust earned through sustained honest service builds influence, while inactivity steadily erodes it. In the EigenTrust-style matrix, freshly spawned identities—whether named marble, inlet, or copper—lack trusted incoming links and thus have near-zero eigenvector centrality. Reciprocity-weighted transitivity cannot bootstrap unsupported links past consensus thresholds, so sybils must earn durable trust rather than merely multiply identities.
